$comment: The catalog's texts in English (components.json has them in Japanese): the same ids. Studio shows these to a page in English (Catalog.InEnglish). Every title, note and description of components.json has its English here (CatalogTests).

noneOption.title: No support
noneOption.description: APIs .NET 10 lacks are stubbed and throw when run. The conversion report lists them.
noneOption.detail: What .NET does not have is stubbed to compile (it throws when run); what it has stays as it is (its exceptions and differences too). Listed in the conversion report

compat.title: Compatible (ResetAbort works)
compat.description: ResetAbort is replaced with a compatible implementation: the code after the catch runs as on .NET Framework.
compat.detail: Thread.ResetAbort is replaced with Platform.ResetAbort: the code after the catch runs as on .NET Framework

none.title: No support
none.description: ResetAbort throws (a 503 in the catch after a redirect, for one).
none.detail: ResetAbort throws (a 503 in the catch after a redirect, for one)

compat.title: Compatible (thread pool)
compat.description: BeginInvoke / EndInvoke are replaced with a compatible implementation.
compat.detail: BeginInvoke / EndInvoke are replaced with FrameworkOnCore.AsyncDelegate

compat-package.title: Compatibility package
compat-package.description: BinaryFormatter is turned on; saved data can be read. Reading untrusted data is dangerous (as on .NET Framework).
compat-package.detail: System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters and EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization. Existing data can be read. Reading untrusted data is dangerous (as on .NET Framework)

framework.title: As .NET Framework (ANSI code page)
framework.description: Returns the original server's encoding: the converter sets it when the sources or pages are in Shift_JIS or another code page; otherwise the OS setting's on Windows, the LANG culture's on Linux.
framework.detail: Encoding.Default is replaced with Platform.DefaultEncoding (the runtime option FrameworkOnCore.AnsiCodePage, which the converter writes with the sources' or pages' code page; else Windows: the OS's setting; Linux: LANG's culture)

none.title: As .NET (UTF-8)
none.description: Files' and hashes' bytes can differ from .NET Framework's.
none.detail: The bytes of files and hashes may differ from .NET Framework's

framework.title: As .NET Framework
framework.description: Doubles and floats become text, and are parsed, with .NET Framework's results.
framework.detail: Doubles and floats made text (ToString, concatenation, interpolation, string.Format, Convert.ToString, Append and Write) go through FrameworkNumbers; Parse, TryParse and TimeSpan.From* through FrameworkParsing. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web writes bound values the same way

none.title: As .NET
none.description: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004 and 2.675 as N2 is 2.67; parsing a number too large gives infinity.
none.detail: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, -0 is "-0", 2.675 as N2 is 2.67; parsing a number too large gives infinity

translations.title: FrameworkOnCore's translations
translations.description: ASP.NET's texts come from FrameworkOnCore's translations (the languages are chosen in Server settings). The wording can differ from Microsoft's language packs.
translations.detail: The texts of System.Web and the other ports (Calendar's titles, Login's labels, Wizard's and GridView's buttons, error pages, the exceptions and messages of ASP.NET AJAX, Chart, ASMX, SqlClient and more) in FrameworkOnCore's own translations (the repository's translations/, MIT), in the languages chosen in the application's setting 'Language packs' (by default the ones the original server had language packs for). The wording may differ from Microsoft's

framework.title: Microsoft's language packs (Windows only)
framework.description: Uses the language packs of the machine that converts (the original wording). Their license does not allow deploying them on Linux.
framework.detail: Satellites made from this machine's .NET Framework language packs (the original server's wording). Microsoft's license forbids distributing them to run on another platform than Windows: only when not deployed on Linux (--deploy none). Microsoft's license terms apply to the deployment

register.title: Register (always)
register.description: Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and the other code pages are registered at startup.
register.detail: FrameworkOnCore's System.Web (UseWebForms) registers CodePagesEncodingProvider at start: Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and the others are there

stderr.title: Standard error on Linux
stderr.description: The event log on Windows; the service's or container's log on Linux.
stderr.detail: The event log on Windows; on Linux, the service's journal or the container's log (FrameworkOnCore.EventLogs)

ef6.title: Move to EF6
ef6.description: Adds the EF6 package, rewrites the namespaces and embeds the EDMX models.
ef6.detail: Adds Entity Framework 6's package, rewrites the namespaces, embeds the EDMX

none.title: No support
none.description: EF4's types are stubbed (they throw when run).

compat.title: Compatible (Windows only)

port.description: Draws with GDI+ on Windows and SkiaSharp on Linux; the deployment installs fontconfig and fonts.

port.detail: System.Data.Linq ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Data.Linq

none.detail: Stubbed. DLLs that reference it (System.Web.Mvc's model binding) throw too

retarget.title: Retarget
retarget.description: The DLLs' references are rewritten to where .NET 10 has the types; the rewritten DLLs are in the output's foc-retargeted.
retarget.detail: The types a DLL without source references as "assembly + type" that .NET 10 has in another assembly (CallContext in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web): the converter retargets the DLL's references to them. Members the type lacks are replaced with calls of the compatibility assembly's extension members. The DLL works as it is (the rewritten DLLs are in the output's foc-retargeted)

none.title: No support
none.description: The DLLs stay as they are; TypeLoadException or MissingMethodException where they use the types.
none.detail: The DLL stays as it is: where it uses those types or members, it throws TypeLoadException or MissingMethodException at run time

port.title: Use the port
port.description: Expands |DataDirectory| to App_Data and accepts Asynchronous Processing and the like; connections opened by Entity Framework or DLLs use it too.
port.detail: FrameworkOnCore's System.Data.SqlClient (package FrameworkOnCore.Data.SqlClient, from dotnet/maintenance-packages 4.9.0's source). It expands |DataDirectory| in connection strings to App_Data as .NET Framework does, and takes Asynchronous Processing, Network Library and Connection Reset, which .NET rejects (SqlConnectionStringBuilder has the properties of those names too). The web project always has it: Entity Framework's connections and the DLLs' are its

port.title: Use the port
port.description: The Chart control and ChartImg.axd work as they are.
port.detail: System.Web.DataVisualization ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.DataVisualization (drawn with the ported System.Drawing: it works on Linux too)

port.title: Use the port
port.description: MobilePage and the mobile: controls work as they are.
port.detail: System.Web.Mobile ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.Mobile (MobilePage, the mobile: controls, the device adapters)

none.title: No support
none.detail: Stubbed (mobile pages throw). A using alone is removed

corewcf.title: Run on CoreWCF
corewcf.description: Supports basicHttpBinding, wsHttpBinding, webHttpBinding (REST) and ASP.NET AJAX (enableWebScript); not netTcpBinding nor custom ServiceHostFactory.
corewcf.detail: The site's .svc services and web.config's system.serviceModel run on CoreWCF within the application (package FrameworkOnCore.ServiceModel): basicHttpBinding, basicHttpsBinding, wsHttpBinding, webHttpBinding (REST), WCF 4's default endpoints and behaviors, serviceActivations, WSDL. The service-side types (ServiceBehavior, WebGet) are rewritten to CoreWCF's. ASP.NET AJAX's enableWebScript too (ScriptManager's ServiceReference, Service.svc/js). Not netTcpBinding, custom ServiceHostFactory, aspNetCompatibilityEnabled (HttpContext.Current in an operation)

none.title: No support
none.description: The services do not run (.svc answers 404).
none.detail: The services do not run (.svc answers 404). The service-side types are stubbed

port.description: Planned: DirectoryEntry and DirectorySearcher working over LDAP on Linux too.

none.detail: Outside Windows, Registry.LocalMachine and the others are null

file.title: A file in its place

file.detail: Planned: Microsoft.Win32.Registry over a file of the values taken from the original server

languages.title: Language packs (the language of ASP.NET's texts)

server.title: As the original server
server.description: Calendar, Login, error pages and the like show in the original server's language-pack languages (when the UI culture is one). Choose English only for English always.
server.detail: English and the languages the original server had .NET Framework language packs for (capture-culture.ps1 records them; else this machine's). When the UI culture is one chosen, Calendar's, Login's, Wizard's and GridView's texts and error pages are in it. English alone: English whatever the UI culture.

insensitive.title: Not distinguished (as Windows)
insensitive.description: On Linux too, files are opened regardless of case, as on Windows.
insensitive.detail: The deployment has casefs (libfoccase.so), which start.sh loads

sensitive.title: Distinguished (Linux's way)
sensitive.description: A file named with a different case than the code uses is not found.
sensitive.detail: A file the application names in another case is not found

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Written in IIS's format and file names (u_exYYMMDD.log), with the original server's settings.
iis.detail: Written as IIS writes it: its format, fields and file names (u_exYYMMDD.log). When writing falls behind, requests wait (no line is dropped). The original server's logFile settings apply

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's W3C log
aspnetcore.description: Its format differs slightly from IIS's, and lines can be dropped under heavy traffic.
aspnetcore.detail: ASP.NET Core's W3CLogger. Its format differs a little from IIS's (no sc-substatus), and it writes up to a limit. It stays as it is once the application is rewritten for ASP.NET Core

off.title: Off
off.description: When a load balancer's log or the like is used.
off.detail: No request log (a load balancer's in front, say)

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: web.config's rewrite rules work as IIS's URL Rewrite does.
iis.detail: The rules run as IIS's URL Rewrite module runs them (inheritance, server variables, Wildcard, the query string's order, redirects' absolute URLs). The original server's globalRules too

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's Rewriter
aspnetcore.description: Some rules work differently from IIS, and a rule it cannot read stops the application from starting.
aspnetcore.detail: ASP.NET Core's rewriting (AddIISUrlRewrite): the root web.config only, some differences from IIS, and the application does not start with rules it cannot read (subStatusCode, Wildcard, some server variables)

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Error answers are replaced as web.config's httpErrors says, as on IIS.
iis.detail: Error answers are replaced as IIS replaces them (errorMode, existingResponse, File, ExecuteURL, Redirect). IIS's own pages are simple ones

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's status code pages
aspnetcore.description: Errors without a body get a short text; the error pages you set are not used.
aspnetcore.detail: A short text for an error without a body. The application's answers are not replaced

off.title: Off
off.description: Errors without a body stay empty.
off.detail: An error without a body stays empty

iis.title: As IIS
iis.description: Compresses as the original server's static and dynamic compression settings say.
iis.detail: Compressed as the original server's static and dynamic compression are set (without its settings, Windows' defaults: a static file gzipped from its second request within 10 seconds)

aspnetcore.title: ASP.NET Core's ResponseCompression
aspnetcore.description: Compresses matching responses every time (not over HTTPS by default).
aspnetcore.detail: Every answer of the types compressed (brotli first; not over HTTPS by default)

off.title: Off
off.description: When a load balancer or a CDN compresses.
off.detail: Left to a load balancer or CDN in front

thread-abort.title: Thread abort (Thread.Abort / ResetAbort)
thread-abort.note: .NET 10 cannot abort threads. With the default, ResetAbort (undoing the abort of Response.End and the like) works as on .NET Framework. Abort is not supported.
thread-abort.detail: Converter: ResetAbort is replaced with Platform.ResetAbort (it undoes the abort of Response.End in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web). Abort is not supported

async-delegates.title: Asynchronous delegate calls (BeginInvoke / EndInvoke)
async-delegates.note: On .NET 10 a delegate's BeginInvoke throws. With the default, the conversion replaces it with a compatible implementation on the thread pool.
async-delegates.detail: Converter: replaced with FrameworkOnCore.AsyncDelegate (run on the thread pool)

binary-formatter.title: BinaryFormatter / SoapFormatter
binary-formatter.note: BinaryFormatter is off on .NET 10 (it throws). With the default, a compatibility package makes it work, and saved data can be read. Reading untrusted data is as dangerous as on .NET Framework.
binary-formatter.detail: Converter: the compatibility package System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters and EnableUnsafeBinaryFormatterSerialization (reading untrusted data is dangerous)

encoding-default.title: Encoding.Default (the default encoding)
encoding-default.note: On .NET Framework Encoding.Default is the OS's ANSI code page (Shift_JIS on a Japanese Windows); on .NET 10 it is UTF-8. With the default, it returns .NET Framework's encoding.
encoding-default.detail: .NET Framework's is the ANSI code page (Shift_JIS on a Japanese Windows), .NET's is UTF-8. Converter: replaced with Platform.DefaultEncoding

floating-point.title: Doubles and floats to and from text
floating-point.note: On .NET 10 doubles become text differently (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004; 2.675 as N2 is 2.67). With the default, ToString, Parse and the like are replaced to give .NET Framework's results.
floating-point.detail: Since .NET Core 3.0 a double without a format is the shortest text that round-trips (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004; .NET Framework: 15 digits, 0.3), negative zero is "-0", a fixed precision rounds the exact binary value to even (2.675 as N2 is 2.67; .NET Framework: 2.68, from its 15 digits). Parsing a number too large gives infinity (.NET Framework: an exception). TimeSpan.FromSeconds(0.00015) and the others are not rounded to milliseconds. Converter: replaced with FrameworkNumbers and FrameworkParsing (FOC1008, platformReplacements)

language-packs.title: .NET Framework language packs (ASP.NET's messages in Japanese and others)
language-packs.note: With a language pack, ASP.NET's texts (Calendar, Login, error pages) were in the server's language. .NET 10 has no language packs. With the default, FrameworkOnCore's translations show them in that language.
language-packs.detail: On a server with a language pack (ja on a Japanese Windows, usually) System.Web's texts are in its language when the UI culture is (Calendar's titles, Login's labels, Wizard's buttons, GridView's commands, error pages). .NET has no language packs. Converter: FrameworkOnCore's own translations (translations/) in the languages of the application's setting 'Language packs' (by default the original server's; Microsoft's packs only when chosen and deployed on Windows only: their license forbids distributing them to run elsewhere). CultureInfo.DisplayName (.NET: in the language of Windows' UI): in a translated language that language's, else the original server's English name (FrameworkCultures)

code-pages.title: Code pages (Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and others)
code-pages.note: .NET 10 has no code pages such as Shift_JIS by default. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web registers them at startup: nothing to choose.
code-pages.detail: Without a registered provider .NET has only Unicode, ASCII and Latin-1. FrameworkOnCore's System.Web (UseWebForms) registers it at start

system-drawing.title: System.Drawing (images and fonts, GDI+)
system-drawing.note: .NET 10's System.Drawing.Common runs on Windows only. It is replaced with a port that runs on Linux too (drawing with SkiaSharp). Anti-aliasing and fonts can render slightly differently.
system-drawing.detail: .NET's System.Drawing.Common is Windows-only since .NET 7. Converter: FrameworkOnCore's System.Drawing.Common (a port with dotnet/runtime 6.0's Linux implementation; on Linux GDI+'s functions over SkiaSharp, libgdiplus, archived, not by default). What it draws (antialiasing, text) differs a little between Windows and Linux. Windows' fonts are not on Linux (Arial and others are replaced with compatible fonts)

charts.title: Charts (the Chart control)
charts.note: The Chart control (System.Web.DataVisualization) is not in .NET 10. A port is used (it draws on Linux too).
charts.detail: Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.DataVisualization (the Chart control, ChartImg.axd). Drawn with the ported System.Drawing (SkiaSharp on Linux). When ChartImg.axd's image folder (appSettings ChartImageHandler's dir) is on C:, the deployment's setting (APPSETTING_ChartImageHandler) changes it on Linux. Windows Forms' System.Windows.Forms.DataVisualization is not ported

sql-client.title: SQL Server client (System.Data.SqlClient)
sql-client.note: .NET 10's System.Data.SqlClient rejects |DataDirectory| and keywords such as Asynchronous Processing in connection strings. A port that accepts them as .NET Framework did is used (ASP.NET's own SQL Server features, SqlDataSource, membership, session state, use it too: Microsoft's cannot be chosen).
sql-client.detail: .NET's System.Data.SqlClient rejects |DataDirectory| in connection strings (.NET Framework expanded it to App_Data). Converter: the port (FrameworkOnCore.Data.SqlClient) expands it as .NET Framework does; FrameworkOnCore's System.Web uses the same port (as .NET Framework's System.Web used the in-box one)

linq-to-sql.title: LINQ to SQL (System.Data.Linq)
linq-to-sql.note: LINQ to SQL is not in .NET 10. A port (for SQL Server) is used.
linq-to-sql.detail: Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Data.Linq (for SQL Server)

entity-framework-4.title: Entity Framework 4 (System.Data.Entity)
entity-framework-4.note: EF4 does not run on .NET 10. With the default, the conversion moves it to the EF6 package and rewrites the namespaces (EDMX models keep working).
entity-framework-4.detail: Converter: moved to EF6 (its package), the namespaces rewritten

wcf-data-services.title: WCF Data Services (OData)
wcf-data-services.note: WCF Data Services is not in .NET 10 and the conversion does not cover it: what uses it has to be rebuilt.
wcf-data-services.todo: Rebuild the OData services and clients (ASP.NET Core OData for the services, Microsoft.OData.Client and the like for the clients).

mobile-controls.title: Mobile controls (System.Web.Mobile)
mobile-controls.note: The mobile controls, deprecated since ASP.NET 4.0. .NET 10 does not have them: a port is used.
mobile-controls.detail: Deprecated in ASP.NET 4.0 (.NET Framework 4.8 has them). Ported from referencesource (MIT): package FrameworkOnCore.Web.Mobile

wcf-server.title: WCF services (ServiceHost, .svc)
wcf-server.note: .NET 10's WCF is the client only. With the default, the .svc files' and web.config's services run on CoreWCF. netTcpBinding and a few others are not supported (the conversion report lists them).
wcf-server.detail: .NET's WCF is the client only. Converter: run on CoreWCF (FrameworkOnCore.ServiceModel registers the .svc and web.config's services with CoreWCF)

wcf-client.title: WCF client (System.ServiceModel)
wcf-client.note: WCF clients run on .NET 10's System.ServiceModel.* packages (some features are missing).
wcf-client.detail: Converter: the System.ServiceModel.* packages (part of the client only)
wcf-client.todo: What uses features .NET 10's WCF client has not got (some bindings and security settings) has to be rebuilt.

event-log.title: The event log (EventLog)
event-log.note: Linux has no event log. With the default, entries go to standard error on Linux (the service's or container's log).

windows-identity.title: Windows accounts and impersonation (WindowsIdentity)
windows-identity.note: Linux has no Windows accounts. With the default, it works on Linux as if there were no account.
windows-identity.detail: Converter: Platform's replacements outside Windows (no account)

file-access-control.title: File and folder access control (ACL)
file-access-control.note: ACL calls such as GetAccessControl work on Windows only; they throw on Linux.
file-access-control.detail: Windows only. Converter: Directory/File.GetAccessControl and the others go to FrameworkOnCore.DirectoryAcl and FileAcl (they throw outside Windows)
file-access-control.todo: On Linux, reading or changing files' and folders' access rights (ACLs) throws. Rewrite checks such as an installer's write permission check to try writing on Linux, or skip them; give the rights at deployment with chmod and chown.

registry.title: The registry (Microsoft.Win32.Registry)
registry.note: Linux has no registry: Registry.LocalMachine and the like are null.
registry.detail: Outside Windows, Registry.LocalMachine and the others are null
registry.todo: Read the values the application takes from the registry (connection strings, folders) from web.config's appSettings or environment variables instead. On a Windows server it runs as it is (with the original server's values in its registry).

oledb.title: OLE DB (reading Excel and Access files)
oledb.note: OLE DB works on Windows only. Linux has no providers: it has to be rewritten another way.
oledb.detail: Windows only: Linux has no provider
oledb.todo: Rewrite where the application reads Excel or Access files through OLE DB. Excel files (.xlsx, .xls) can be read with a library such as ExcelDataReader; for Access files, moving the data to SQL Server or the like is the safe way. On a Windows server it runs as it is (with the Microsoft Access Database Engine installed).

directory-services.title: Active Directory (System.DirectoryServices)
directory-services.note: System.DirectoryServices works on Windows only. On Linux it has to be rewritten with LDAP (System.DirectoryServices.Protocols).
directory-services.detail: Windows only. Needs a rewrite to LDAP (System.DirectoryServices.Protocols)
directory-services.todo: Rewrite the queries to Active Directory (DirectoryEntry, DirectorySearcher) with LdapConnection (System.DirectoryServices.Protocols), which runs on Linux too. On a Windows server it runs as it is.

windows-management.title: WMI, performance counters, Windows services
windows-management.todo: Reading the server's information (WMI) or performance figures (performance counters) and controlling Windows services do not work on Linux. Remove them if they are not needed; otherwise rewrite them the Linux way (/proc's files, .NET's metrics, systemctl).

code-access-security.title: Code access security (CAS)
code-access-security.note: .NET 10 ignores it (no partial trust). Web applications usually run in full trust, so this rarely matters.
code-access-security.detail: .NET does nothing with it (there is no partial trust). Web applications usually run in full trust

app-domains.title: Creating AppDomains (AppDomain.CreateDomain)
app-domains.note: .NET 10 has one AppDomain only: code that creates more has to be rewritten.
app-domains.todo: Rewrite where the application creates AppDomains: AssemblyLoadContext to load plug-ins, a separate process to isolate.

remoting.title: Remoting (System.Runtime.Remoting)
remoting.note: .NET Remoting is not in .NET 10. FrameworkOnCore provides only some parts (CallContext and the like).
remoting.detail: Not in .NET. Some of it (CallContext) is in FrameworkOnCore's System.Web and the compatibility assembly
remoting.todo: Rewrite what talks over .NET Remoting with HTTP (Web API and the like) or gRPC.

code-dom-compile.title: Compiling at run time (CodeDom)
code-dom-compile.note: .NET 10's CodeDom generates code only; compiling throws.
code-dom-compile.detail: .NET's CodeDom does not compile (it throws); it generates code only
code-dom-compile.todo: Compiling sources at run time (CodeDomProvider.CompileAssemblyFromSource and the like) throws. Rewrite it with Roslyn (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp).

web-request.title: WebRequest / WebClient
web-request.note: Obsolete on .NET 10 but working (HttpClient is recommended).
web-request.detail: Obsolete in .NET but works (HttpClient is recommended)

legacy-crypto.title: Old cryptography classes (*CryptoServiceProvider, *Managed)
legacy-crypto.note: Obsolete on .NET 10 but working (only Rijndael with BlockSize 256 throws).
legacy-crypto.detail: Obsolete in .NET but works (Rijndael's BlockSize 256 throws)

designers.title: Designers and Windows Forms
designers.note: Types for Visual Studio's designers. Not needed to run: the conversion stubs them or removes them from web.config.
designers.detail: For Visual Studio's designers. Converter: stubbed, removed from web.config
designers.todo: Usually nothing (these types are for Visual Studio's design time only). Remove any code that uses them at run time.

web-forms.title: ASP.NET (System.Web: Web Forms, ASMX and others)
web-forms.note: System.Web is not in .NET 10; FrameworkOnCore has a version that runs on it.
web-forms.detail: FrameworkOnCore (System.Web and the others, from WebFormsForCore) has them for .NET

configuration.title: Configuration (System.Configuration)
configuration.note: Reading web.config and the like works with FrameworkOnCore's .NET 10 version.

visual-basic-runtime.title: The Visual Basic runtime (Microsoft.VisualBasic)
visual-basic-runtime.note: .NET 10 has it (Microsoft.VisualBasic.Core). Parts of My and the like come from the compatibility assembly.
visual-basic-runtime.detail: .NET's Microsoft.VisualBasic.Core. Some of My's types are in the compatibility assembly

dll-references.title: References from DLLs without source
dll-references.note: A DLL without source refers to a type by assembly and type name. On .NET 10 the type can be in another assembly. With the default, the conversion rewrites the DLL's references so that it works.
dll-references.detail: A DLL without source references a type as "assembly + type"; these are types .NET 10 has in another assembly (which ones: APIs; each API is counted in its own component too)
